title: Investigate pinned host-staging oscillation causing steady GPU RSS growth under continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Production inference pools with continuous batching enabled show a slow but steady increase in GPU resident set and host pinned memory over 24+ hour runs. Pattern emerges when KV prefetch is enabled and workloads have many small lookups (tail latencies low, throughput high). Symptoms: rising RSS on GPU (nvidia-smi), increase in host pinned pages, and longer contagion of cudaFree completion times in logs. This ticket tracks root-cause tracing, short-term mitigations, and permanent fixes to allocator/free-path behavior.
steps_taken: Created small repro harness that simulates continuous batching with synthetic prompts and randomized KV prefetch sizes (256B-16KB) - repo: github.com/redwood/repro/eng/ENG-523581
Collected heap snapshots from the runtime with MALLOC_TRIM, jemalloc stats, and custom allocator counters at 1h intervals
Enabled CUpti/cudaMemGetInfo sampling and captured per-stream allocation histograms for 12h on a busy Dedicated cluster node
Instrumented allocator metadata to log stream_id, arena_id, allocation_size, and event fence timestamps for allocations > 512 bytes
Pulled node telemetry (prometheus): allocator.free_latency_seconds_bucket, cuda_async_pending_events, host_pinned_bytes, gpu_resident_bytes over 72h
hypotheses: Pinned host-staging allocations are being created as a fallback when device pool allocation misses; these pinned allocations are not returned promptly because their free-work is queued on a stream that frequently stalls under continuous batching.

cudaMallocAsync per-stream arena trim callbacks are not firing due to backpressure: event callbacks are scheduled on the same streams used for inference, and long-running batches block trimming, preventing return-to-OS or to fallback pools.
Small, highly fragmented allocation sizes from KV prefetch cause slab internal fragmentation and keep many arenas partially occupied, preventing full slab reclamation.

An interaction between our KV prefetch concurrency and allocator's async-decommit watermark causes constant churn between device and host-staging pools leading to oscillating pinned memory peaks and gradual leak-like residue.

Race condition in deferred-free queue where remote stream frees are delayed by a misordered event fence, leaving allocations in 'quarantine' until stream drain which can be arbitrarily delayed under load.
findings: Reproducer shows steady host_pinned_bytes growth when concurrent prefetch threads >= 8 with average prefetch size < 8KB. Lower concurrency or larger prefetch sizes reduce growth rate.

Per-stream histograms show many small allocations pinned to worker streams and frees posted to a central 'reclaim' stream; drains for the reclaim stream are delayed by ~50-200ms under peak batching windows, accumulating queued frees.
Allocator internal metrics show deferred_free_queue length correlates with host_pinned_bytes spikes. When queue length > 10k entries, pinned memory climbs until manual throttle applied.

nvtx traces reveal event callbacks used by cudaMallocAsync trim are scheduled on the inference streams; when a stream runs long microbatches, the trim callback latency spikes and the allocator does not trim arenas.

No evidence of a kernel-level driver leak; cudaMemReport and driver traces show allocations are accounted for but release timing is delayed, causing effective growth in resident set until eventual reclamation.

Captured one reproducible race where an allocation's free fence was signaled on the wrong stream in a rare code-path when fallback host staging was used concurrently with prefetch cancellation; this caused the allocation to remain 'reachable' by the allocator's arena and not be recycled.
Pinned staging pool size increases as allocator prefers returning small freed device blocks to host staging instead of merging them into larger device arenas when fragmentation thresholds are high.
short_term_mitigations: Throttle KV prefetch concurrency by default in the runtime config (max_prefetch_concurrency: 4) to reduce small-allocation tail under load. Deployed to canary pool on 2025-11-06.
Increase host-staging pool cap per-GPU temporarily to avoid OOMs while we instrument deeper (staging_pool_cap_bytes: +25%).

Enable an emergency background 'free-runner' thread per node that consumes deferred_free_queue and uses a dedicated reclaim stream to process frees even if worker streams are busy. (Patch applied behind flag: runtime.free_runner_enabled=true)
Add temporary alert: allocator.deferred_free_queue_length > 2000 -> page on oncall and auto-throttle prefetch rate for affected node.
proposed_long_term_fixes: Offload all allocator trimming and free processing to a dedicated reintegrator thread/stream to avoid relying on worker streams for critical trims.
Change host-staging allocation policy: prefer coalesced staging for many small prefetches by aggregating small KV prefetch requests into a single backed pinned buffer, reducing slab fragmentation.
Introduce adaptive trim thresholds for cudaMallocAsync arenas based on observed stream stall percentiles and deferred_free_queue growth; tune to proactively trim when drain latency rises.

Fix the identified free-fence race by auditing fallback paths and ensuring frees always attach fences to the reclaim stream. Add unit tests that simulate concurrent cancellation, fallback, and prefetch interleaving.
Add allocator-level metrics: per-arena fragmentation ratio, scheduled_trims_pending, last_trim_latency_millis for observability and runbook automation
Experiment with small-allocation coalescer in the KV prefetcher to group many <4KB prefetches into single device allocations with internal indexing, evaluate latency trade-offs.
Roll out phased canaries and monitor: runtime-1.22 with reclamation-thread and adaptive-trim (canary -> 5% -> 25% -> full).
next_steps: Create PR with reclaim-thread implementation and unit/integration tests (ENG-523581/reclaim-thread) - target: 2025-11-14
Prototype coalescer in KV prefetcher as opt-in flag; bench memory usage and p50/p95 latency impact - assigned to @anika-s (research pairing)
Add new Prometheus gauges and alerts for allocator.per_arena_fragmentation and allocator.last_trim_latency - infra ticket INF-1187
Schedule runtime perf run against Dedicated cluster using 4xA100, run 24h stable workload with continuous batching to validate regression on memory slope
Prepare rollout plan and runbook covering emergency rollback (disable reclaim-thread, revert prefetch throttle), include postmortem template.
